newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares stage technical recovery.
newsitem.headline: French shares stage technical recovery.

text.p: French shares rose smartly in early trade on Tuesday in what dealers described as a technical recovery after Monday's big drop before shading back their gains.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index jumped nearly one percent at the start of dealing before falling back to trade up 0.47 percent at 3,006.61 at midmorning in modest August summer holiday volume. Volume on the CAC-40 totalled 760 million francs.
Dealers said the market remained wary about the possibility of interest rate tightening in Germany to stem the mark's fall against the dollar.

There was also concern about a rate hike in the United States after recent strong economic data. But dealers said Wall Street's slim overnight gains, shrugging off the bond market's weakness, gave some reassurance to the French investors on Tuesday.
"The market is still very nervous. People are worried that the Bundesbank will raise rates," said one dealer. He added that the market was ready to "punish any negative news pretty severely."

Among the gainers, Cie Bancaire was up 1.96 percent at 779 francs after announcing the sale of 4.7 billion francs of real estate loans on the books of UCB Bank to Birmingham Mildshires Building Societ.
Primagaz was off 6.45 percent at 493 francs after forecasting a pre-tax, pre-exceptional first half profit down 30 percent.
